cards.intuition: The cheapest recall fix in RAG: one small model call translates user-speak into corpus-speak before search ever runs.
cards.formula: raw query -> rewrite -> retrieve; keep raw as fallback
cards.topic: Single-Shot Query Rewriting, Expansion, and HyDE

cards.intuition: Write a fake answer, embed it, and search near it. The facts may be wrong, but the neighborhood is usually right, until the query is a precise lookup.
cards.formula: embed(hypothetical answer) is near embed(real answers)
cards.topic: Single-Shot Query Rewriting, Expansion, and HyDE

cards.intuition: Retrieval becomes a tool the model can call again: search, read the best hits, then decide whether the evidence is enough.
cards.formula: while evidence insufficient and budget remains: search/read
cards.topic: Retrieval as a Tool: Search, Read, Decide-to-Stop

cards.intuition: Coverage of the question's facets, the marginal utility of another search, and a hard budget decide when to answer. The cap is what prevents runaway loops.
cards.formula: stop when facets covered or budget spent
cards.topic: Retrieval as a Tool: Search, Read, Decide-to-Stop

cards.intuition: Each hop's retrieval success multiplies down the chain, so three 90 percent hops deliver only about 73 percent before any reasoning errors.
A wrong entity in hop one poisons the query for hop two, and the chain walks off a cliff with full confidence.
cards.formula: wrong hop-1 answer -> poisoned hop-2 query

cards.intuition: Rewrite the latest turn into a standalone query using recent history and the last assistant answer, then search with the standalone form.
When the user changes topic, stale entities leak into the rewrite. The fix is one instruction: standalone turns pass through unchanged.
cards.formula: if turn already standalone: return unchanged

cards.intuition: Grade the retrieval before answering and re-retrieve on failure; grade the draft's claims against the context after writing and refine or abstain.
cards.formula: retrieve -> grade -> maybe re-retrieve -> draft -> check support

cards.intuition: After the attempt budget is spent, a caveated answer or a clean cannot-verify beats a fluent fabrication, especially in support products.
cards.formula: budget spent -> answer with caveats or abstain

cards.intuition: Some questions need rows, not chunks. The model writes SQL from the question plus schema context, and the returned rows become the answer's evidence.
cards.topic: Text-to-SQL as a Retrieval Tool for Structured Data

cards.intuition: Link the schema, ground the values against real column contents, and execute only validated read-only single SELECTs with row limits and timeouts.
cards.topic: Text-to-SQL as a Retrieval Tool for Structured Data
